text: Every Copy activity, every Lookup, every data flow this entire course has built so far has genuinely run on the Azure integration runtime — Data Factory's own AutoResolveIntegrationRuntime, created automatically the moment you made a new data factory. You never provisioned it, never patched it, never sized it. That's genuinely the whole point.

The Azure IR provides real serverless compute in Azure — no infrastructure to provision, no software to patch, no capacity to plan ahead of time. For a Copy activity, you set data integration units, a measure of the power you actually want available, and the underlying compute scales elastically to match, with no manual resizing required at all.

Autoresolve genuinely doesn't mean random — it follows a real, predictable pattern. A Copy activity with a detectable sink location runs in that sink's own region, or the closest one nearby. Lookup, GetMetadata, and Delete activities always run in the data factory's own region. And data flows follow that same rule.

Some real projects have genuinely strict data compliance requirements — data that simply can't leave a specific geography. For those, create an explicit, regional Azure IR, and point a linked service at it directly with connectVia. Copying between two resources both pinned to the same regional IR guarantees the data never actually leaves that region — autoresolve's best-effort detection alone isn't a strong enough guarantee for that kind of requirement.

Managed, serverless, and predictable once you actually understand the rules behind it. Next: Self-Hosted Integration Runtime — installing the real bridge to data the Azure IR simply can't reach on its own.
